Senses.Explanation: “Open your mouth and you are already wrong” is spoken as both self-verdict and interview challenge, commonly paired with losing by silence or missing as soon as the mind frames an answer. Literally, open the mouth and immediately or already be wrong : "open your mouth and you are already wrong." The phrase occurs 43 times in 34 allowlisted texts; the variant "open your mouth and it is then wrong" occurs 13 times in 10. Its early defining exchange has an unnamed questioner ask Dabe to speak apart from removing the upper and taking away the lower. Dabe answers, "when I open my mouth I am already wrong" . The unnamed questioner calls Dabe his guide; Dabe replies, "today I died in the disciple's hands" , so the record shows the verdict catching Dabe’s own utterance. Later masters make it a portable paired formula: Po'an says, "open your mouth and you are already wrong; aim the mind and you immediately miss" . Other records pair it with "move a thought and immediately go against" . Wuzhun states the closed-mouth counterpart, "open your mouth and you are already wrong; close your mouth and you are already lost," then asks how communication is possible apart from opening and not opening . The phrase also becomes an encounter instruction: Baishan tells an unnamed questioner, "open your mouth and you are already wrong; move a thought and immediately go against; leave these two roads and speak quickly!" The unnamed questioner answers, "wrong," and Baishan answers with another stock retort. Chan thus bends an ordinary judgment of erroneous speech into a self-applying verdict, a fixed parallel line, and a demand used while requiring an answer; the records preserve the resulting replies rather than defining silence as the solution.
